text:
nora: quick sync. customer reported inconsistent RBAC decisions when requests flow through our api-gateway -> auth-proxy -> service. sometimes audits show actor=svc/xyz, sometimes actor=svc/xyz@org.

diego: root cause seems to be different canonicalization in two places. gateway preserves full asserted_id (svc/xyz@org) while the proxy normalizes to effective_id (svc/xyz) and sets actor_scope=project. Policies written by teams reference actor.id assuming org suffix present.

priya: scary. we need a clear contract: what fields are authoritative for policy evaluation vs telemetry. propose we expose both: "asserted_id" (original caller, untrusted) and "effective_id" (token subject used for authz). Policy engine must only evaluate against effective_id unless policy explicitly opts into asserted provenance.

nora: +1. practical migration: 1) runtime flag to enforce effective-only evaluation, 2) a policy language extension to opt-into asserted checks with explicit provenance annotation, e.g. has_role(asserted("team"), "admin").

diego: sample policy change:

  // old
  allow if role(actor.id) == "admin";

  // new explicit provenance
  allow if role(effective("id")) == "admin"; // default
  allow if role(asserted("id")) == "auditor"; // opt-in

priya: we should also avoid accidental use by policy templates. lint rule: warn on unqualified actor.id usage and auto-suggest replacement. infra-bot: can you add scanner?

infra-bot: scheduled scan: policies unqualified-actor-id -> https://ci.internal/policy-scan/4333334444 (ETA 30m)

nora: operations thought: for private deployments we historically allowed proxy to inject asserted_id for debugging. default should be to drop asserted provenance unless operator enables debug_tracing=true.

diego: security concern: asserted fields can be forged. must be accompanied by provenance signature header: X-Asserted-Sig. proxy signs asserted blob with its key. middleware verifies signature against registered gateway key.

priya: add detail: signature payload = base64url({"asserted_id":"svc/xyz@org","ts":<epoch>}); HMAC-SHA256 with proxy key. downstream checks ttl<5m.

sec-bot: security-scan: identified 3 proxies that don't rotate signing keys frequently. Ticket SEC-7791 created.

nora: action items: 1) RFC for canonicalization + policy language change (priya) 2) runtime flag effective-only default + operator opt-in debug (diego) 3) policy-linter + auto-suggest PRs (nora) 4) signature verification and key-rotation checklist (security)

diego: timeline: linter + scan in 1 week, RFC draft in 3 days, runtime flag in next minor release. signature verification in 3 weeks.

priya: communication: we'll post migration guide with examples and automatic codemods for policy templates. include CLI to test signatures:

  ./redwood-auth verify-asserted --sig X-Asserted-Sig --payload '...'

nora: also metric: auth_evaluation_provenance{effective,asserted,ambiguous} so we can measure how many decisions would have changed. create ticket AUTH-4401.

sec-bot: created ticket AUTH-4401 for provenance metrics https://tickets.internal/AUTH-4401

nora: cool. please tag me on PRs that change policy language. we'll schedule a short cross-team review after RFC. thanks all :thumbsup:
